einzeiler: Why creative achievement leaves us feeling empty and how the act of making sustains us.
kurzfassung: Creative achievements often bring only a fleeting sense of joy and accomplishment that quickly fades away. Interviews with numerous artists and creators reveal that the true reward lies in the ongoing act of creation itself rather than external validation. Embracing the creative process rather than chasing peaks helps prevent post-project despair.
stichpunkte: The feeling of pride after completing a major project is remarkably short-lived for many creative people.
Interviews with poets, designers, and musicians show that fulfillment usually ends as soon as the work is finished.
Society's obsession with metrics, awards, and visibility creates a culture built around superficial achievement.
True creative satisfaction comes from answering an inner calling to build and express rather than seeking external rewards.
The act of making functions like essential oxygen for creators, whereas reaching the top can feel isolated and cold.
Celebrating wins with collaborators and marking personal milestones helps ease the emotional dip following a major project.

clips.text: A well-known painter confessed that her sense of satisfaction following the opening of a major exhibition lasted barely longer than ten minutes.
A massively successful album sold millions of copies and dominated the charts while narrowly missing the top spot due to a release from Michael Jackson.
Reaching the absolute summit of one's profession turns out to be an isolating and chilly experience where progress can only move downward.
Following a demanding production schedule, the entire crew extended their time together through multiple group dinners because they were not ready to part ways.
Securing a major professional milestone was commemorated by turning the exact calendar date into a permanent annual recurring reminder.

beschreibung:
Over two decades of interviewing countless creative people, Debbie Millman (host of the iconic "Design Matters" podcast) had a realization: the pride and joy of accomplishing something often evaporates almost instantly. She explains how to stop chasing external validation for your achievements and instead live for the act of creation itself. After, Modupe shares how she finds time to celebrate after the end of every project.
